Priya Shah: quick follow-up from yesterday's RFC thread — we still need to pick where RBAC checks happen for snapshot routing and tile reads. i sketched two options. :thinking:
Alex Kim: yea we talked about this but not concretely. can you paste the tradeoffs?
Priya Shah: Option A: pushdown authz into tile reader (fast path). pros: avoids extra hop, can short-circuit per-tile decisions, lower p99. cons: duplicates policy code, harder to audit, cache poisoning risk if policy changes but tiles cached.
Sam Ortiz: Option B being centralized gate in front of query multiplexer? we've historically favored central policy to keep single source of truth.
Priya Shah: exactly. Option B pros: single place to audit and change rules, simpler cache invalidation model. cons: extra network hop and possible extra serialization of requests -> higher tail latency.
Marta Li: what about a hybrid: central decision for tenant/global policies, pushdown for immutable snapshot-level allow/deny? like compute immutable grants when snapshot is created and attach to snapshot metadata.
Alex Kim: hybrid seems attractive. question: how do we keep snapshot grants from getting stale when orgs change roles? we can't accept long-lived stale grants for enterprise customers.
Priya Shah: thought about that — proposal: snapshot has a short-lived derived token (TTL 1h) plus a last-updated epoch. on read, tile reader validates epoch against central service; if mismatch, it rejects and lets multiplexer recheck. this keeps fast-path valid most of the time and allows revocation within TTL.
Sam Ortiz: TTL-based revocation is pragmatic. need to measure revocation visibility worst-case. what's acceptable? 1h might be too long for some compliance customers.
Marta Li: we could make TTL configurable per-tenant (enterprise contracts) and default to 5m for orgs that require faster revoke. configurable adds complexity but ok.
Alex Kim: ok but complexity-wise, we must ensure derived token verification is cheap and cache-friendly. also need to avoid per-request central calls for every tile.
Priya Shah: exactly — flow would be: 1) central policy service issues derived token at snapshot build time with epoch. 2) tile reader validates signature locally (no network call) and checks epoch vs ephemeral epoch cache. 3) only on epoch miss do we hit central to fetch latest epoch. So common-case zero extra hop.
Sam Ortiz: add to backlog: implement an epoch cache with singleflight to avoid thundering herd on expiry.
Alex Kim: how does this interact with caching/tiling lifecycle? if we evict tiles, how do we ensure newly read tiles get the correct derived token?
Priya Shah: when tiles are (re)materialized we attach the current derived token metadata as part of the tile manifest. manifests are signed and immutable.
Marta Li: sounds good but watch out for tile federation: a tile might be composed from multiple tenants' snapshots in some cross-tenant queries. do we expect that?
Priya Shah: at present console queries are tenant-scoped; cross-tenant composition is not supported for snapshots. if that changes we'll need a different approach.
Alex Kim: operational concerns: metrics and SLOs. what do we measure?
Priya Shah: 1) extra p99 added by central-gate fallback path, 2) token-expiry-caused retries, 3) epoch-miss rate, 4) authz-failure rate and false positives.
Sam Ortiz: also monitor cache hit ratio for derived-token cache and singleflight contention.
Marta Li: rollout plan?
Priya Shah: propose phased rollout:
- Phase 1 (dev): implement derived token generation + local signature validation in tile reader, default TTL=5m for all orgs in dev. wire up metrics.
- Phase 2 (canary): enable hybrid for 10% of production tenants (low-traffic), TTL=1h, monitor metric set for 48h.
- Phase 3 (gradual): expand canary while adding tenant-config TTL flag and admin revoke API.
- Phase 4 (opt-in enterprise): enable per-tenant TTL controls, add audit hooks for policy changes.
Alex Kim: rollback plan? if we see authz failures spike, we revert tile-reader validation and fallback to central-gate only. that should be a single feature-flag flip.
Sam Ortiz: anything else re: SLOs? table of alerting thresholds would help.
Priya Shah: put draft thresholds: auth-failure rate >0.05% -> p1; epoch-miss rate >2% -> investigate; fallback latency p95 > baseline+30ms -> p1. open to adjusting.
Marta Li: what about consistency guarantees for staleness when snapshot materialization and role change happen concurrently? race window exists where snapshot created then org access removed immediately. derived token TTL means short window where access might persist. need explicit contract in docs.
Priya Shah: agreed. we'll document that revocation has a worst-case visibility of TTL and ensure enterprise contracts can set TTL near-zero for stricter needs (and accept performance/more central calls).
Alex Kim: security review needed: have security review the signature scheme and key rotation. also KMS integration for signing keys.
Sam Ortiz: infra-bot note: created infra ticket INFRA-1223 to add singleflight epoch cache + metrics.
infra-bot: ticket INFRA-1223 created by Priya Shah — "epoch-cache singleflight and metrics for derived-token validation".
Priya Shah: next steps: i'll write a short follow-up RFC with diagrams, a simple state machine for derived token lifecycle, and the staged rollout. please add comments inline. @Alex Kim @Sam Ortiz can you two review the security and rollout sections? :eyes:
Alex Kim: will review by EOD.
Sam Ortiz: I'll take the infra section.
eng-oncall: ping — if this hits production we should add a perf run in staging to catch regressions, ping me when canary starts.
Priya Shah: thanks — tagging eng-oncall check in the rollout. will push RFC by tomorrow morning. :shipit:
